forecasting.title: Restaurant Inventory Forecasting Capstone
forecasting.summary: A Python package plus Streamlit dashboard that runs a full planning workflow: load restaurant data, forecast menu demand, convert it through recipe mappings, evaluate stock risk, and draft supplier reorders.

architecture.label: Pipeline orchestration
architecture.detail: run_pipeline wires loaders, RidgeDemandForecaster, ingredient conversion, inventory alerts, supplier reorders, draft messages, and mapping coverage into one result object.

architecture.label: Forecasting model
architecture.detail: RidgeDemandForecaster builds calendar, restaurant, menu, weather, promotion, pricing, and event features, then solves ridge regression with NumPy.

architecture.label: Inventory logic
architecture.detail: Inventory logic is deterministic: historical ingredient usage, synthetic missing ingredient inventory, days of cover, lead-time demand, reorder quantity, supplier grouping, and draft email generation.

architecture.label: Dashboard layer
architecture.detail: Streamlit exposes scenario controls, CSV uploads, Quick Stock Update state, forecast charts, stock health, supplier orders, and downloadable CSV outputs.

pipeline: CSV loaders validate and normalize sales, inventory, recipe mapping, and supplier contact schemas.
RidgeDemandForecaster performs a time-based holdout evaluation and forecasts menu demand for a configurable horizon.
Forecasted menu quantities are joined to recipe_mapping and multiplied by quantity_per_order.
Stock alerts compare effective daily usage, current stock, reorder level, and supplier lead time.
Recommended reorder quantities are grouped by supplier and rendered as summary tables plus draft order emails.
logicSplit: Machine learning is isolated to menu-level sales forecasting.
Ingredient conversion, stock health, reorder quantities, supplier routing, and draft messages are rule-based business logic.

metrics.label: Forecast metrics
metrics.detail: Computed through a time-based holdout split in RidgeDemandForecaster.evaluate.

metrics.label: Tests
metrics.detail: Smoke tests cover workflow integration and inventory invariants.

dashboard.alt: Streamlit central warehouse planning dashboard showing demand, stock issues, reorder spend, and supplier drafts.
dashboard.caption: Actual Streamlit dashboard capture from the forecasting project.

workflow.label: Sales history
workflow.detail: Menu-level demand by date, restaurant, weather, promotions, pricing, and event flags.

workflow.label: Ridge forecast
workflow.detail: The only ML stage: a simple, debuggable demand forecast for menu item quantities.

workflow.label: Recipe mapping
workflow.detail: Forecasted dishes are converted into ingredient requirements using quantity_per_order.

workflow.label: Stock health
workflow.detail: Current stock is compared against usage, reorder levels, and supplier lead time.

workflow.label: Supplier plan
workflow.detail: Items are grouped into reorder recommendations and draft supplier messages.

crowdDetection.title: CrowdDetection Stage 2
crowdDetection.summary: A modular PyTorch crowd-counting codebase that separates density-map generation, datasets, CSRNet variants, training, evaluation, checkpointing, and report-ready comparison outputs.

architecture.label: Baseline model
architecture.detail: CSRNetBaseline uses a VGG16-style frontend, a dilated backend, and a 1-channel density head for fair reproduction.

architecture.label: Advanced model
architecture.detail: AdvancedCSRNet adds MultiScaleContextBlock, residual dilated blocks, CBAM channel/spatial attention, dropout, batch norm, and a refined density head.

architecture.label: Count-consistency loss
architecture.detail: CrowdCountingLoss combines density MSE with optional L1 count loss after shape matching preserves predicted count mass.

architecture.label: Training engine
architecture.detail: The trainer handles AMP, gradient clipping, schedulers, checkpoint snapshots, best metrics, sample analysis, and density breakdown exports.

pipeline: Generate ShanghaiTech density maps from point annotations with KDTree-informed Gaussian smoothing.
Load count-preserving resized/downsampled density maps through ShanghaiTechCrowdDataset.
Train CSRNetBaseline and AdvancedCSRNet from JSON configs with identical split structure.
Track MAE, RMSE, PSNR, SSIM, density loss, count loss, and sample-level density bands.
Compare baseline and advanced output folders into report-ready metric tables.

metrics.label: Advanced RMSE
metrics.detail: Reported from repository output JSON, not invented.

deepfake.title: Deepfake Detection
deepfake.summary: A notebook-based video deepfake detection experiment that builds a FaceForensics++ C23 frame index, splits by video to avoid leakage, trains EfficientNet-B0 and ResNet50, evaluates frame/video metrics, and exports a Gradio inference notebook.

architecture.label: Frame sampling
architecture.detail: Videos are converted into frame-level rows using evenly spaced frame indices; large frame caches are avoided.

architecture.label: Anti-leakage split
architecture.detail: GroupShuffleSplit separates train and validation by video_id so frames from the same video do not appear in both splits.

architecture.label: Model experiments
architecture.detail: EfficientNet-B0 and ResNet50 are trained with BCEWithLogitsLoss and compared using frame-level and video-level metrics.

architecture.label: Inference UI
architecture.detail: The Gradio UI loads model_final_meta.json and model_final.pt, samples frames, optionally crops faces, averages p(fake), and applies the tuned threshold.

pipeline: Find video files and infer real/fake labels from FaceForensics++ folder structure.
Sample frame indices per video and persist train/validation CSVs.
Decode frames lazily with OpenCV and optionally crop the largest detected face.
Train EfficientNet-B0 and ResNet50 with frame-level binary classification.
Aggregate frame probabilities by video, tune a threshold by balanced accuracy, and export evaluation artifacts.

headings: 4. Build labeled video index (real vs fake)
6. Frame sampling plan (create frame-level samples, split by video)

workflow.label: Video-level split
workflow.detail: Train and validation are separated by video_id to avoid frame leakage.

workflow.label: Model comparison
workflow.detail: EfficientNet-B0 and ResNet50 are evaluated on frame and video metrics.

workflow.label: Inference aggregation
workflow.detail: Frame probabilities are averaged into a video-level probability and thresholded.
